DILG Republic or the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, woot Triangle, Quezon City http dilg.gov.ph OPINION NO_ Lil 1 9 SEP s. 2013 MR. ERWIN B. DELA TORRE President Rising Star Cable TV Services 127 Lourdes St., Buenmar Pasig City Dear Mr. Dela Torre: This is in reference to your letter dated 27 July 2017, stating among others that you filed an application (with complete requirements) for business permit on 18 August 2016 before the Business Permits and Licensing Office (BPLO) of Lucena City, Quezon for the operation of Cable TV (CAT V) services. However, to date, no business permit has been issued on the ground that you did not obtain the endorsement of the Sangguninang Panlungsod as the latter, allegedly, is empowered to enact ordinances granting franchises. Perusal of the records by this Office shows that this issue was already addressed by this Department in its letter dated 23 January 2017 to Mayor Alcala. However, despite said letter, it appears that you were not granted the business permit on the same ground, that is the endorsement by the Sanggunian was not obtained. Hence, this Department, again, sent a letter to Mayor Alcala reiterating the policy and applicable laws in the issuance of business permits. If it is your belief that the local government of Lucena City violated certain laws like Republic Act No. 9485, otherwise known as the "Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007" and/or other related laws and issuances, you may file a corresponding civil, criminal and administrative complaint against the erring officials with either to the Civil Service Commission (CSC), the Presidential Anti-Graft Commission (PAGC) or the Office of the Ombudsman by virtue of Sections 13 and 14 of RA No. 9485, to wit: "SEC. 13. Civil and Criminal Liability, Not Barred. - The finding of administrative liability under this Act shall not be a bar to the filing of criminal, civil or other related charges under existing la arising from the same act or omission as herein enumerated. SEC. 14. Administrative Jurisdiction. - The administrative jurisdiction on any violation of the provisions of this Act shall be vested in either the Civil Service Commission (CSC), the Presidential Anti-Graft•

Commission (PA GC) or the Office of the Ombudsman as determined by appropriate laws and issuances. " The provision stated above is in harmony with the DILG-DTI Joint Memorandum Circular No. I, S. 2016 dated 30 August 2016, viz: "10. O Enforcement Cla use This Joint Memorandum Circular shall enforce all the provisions of Republic Act No. 9485 or Anti-red Tape Act of 2007 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations, DILG Memorandum Circular 2011-15 and COA Circular 2013-007. " Alternatively, the complaint may also be filed with the following, as provided in Section 61 of the Local Government Code: "Form and Filing of Administrative Complaints. - A verified complaint against any erring local elective official shall be prepared as follows: (a) A complaint against any elective official ofa province, a highly urbanized city, an independent component city or component city shall be filed before the Office of the President; (b) A complaint against any elective official ofa municipality shall be filed before the sangguniang panlalawigan whose decision may be appealed to the Office of the President; " We thank you for referring your concern to us and we hope that we were able to enlighten you on the matter. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary CC: Dir. Manuel Q. Gotis OIC-Regional Director DILG-Region IV-A (CALABARZON)
